required_changes: Complete Q1 and the mapped source finding for successful setup. The pinned save guide returns the SetupIntent client secret for stripe.confirmSetup and uses the saved PaymentMethod ID on the later on-session PaymentIntent (old raw lines 50-62 and new raw lines 47-57). Clarify that the caller verifies the SetupIntent result and its saved PaymentMethod before treating the method as available for reuse, keeping return navigation distinct from successful setup or a purchase. The separately dated general Elements save guide documents retrieving the SetupIntent with the client secret, inspecting status, and successful confirmation saving the resulting PaymentMethod to the Customer (raw/stripe-save-and-reuse-elements-2025.md:946-953,967-986); the November Stripe.js retrieve reference corroborates the client-secret lookup (raw/stripe-js-setup-intents-retrieve-setup-intent-2026-11-07.md:5-12). Scope this as companion guidance, not a new meal-voucher-specific response contract.

In Q2 and the mapped assessment, make the missing HTTP header risk concrete. The November save guide requires API version 2026-05-27.preview or later, while both raw HTTP snippets omit Stripe-Version (new raw lines 25-29,39-45,61-71). The cited SDK/version documentation says raw requests without Stripe-Version use the account's default API version (raw/stripe-sdks-set-version-2026-11-07.md:5-17). Explain that the documented preview API version must actually be selected and can be targeted with an explicit Stripe-Version header for the HTTP samples when the default does not meet it. Keep it scoped to the API contract, without claiming any particular SDK release or preview entitlement.
